assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new class of quantum matter: insulating bulk with protected conducting edge or surface states, a clear discovery of new quantum behaviour in materials. Theory (Z2 invariant, quantum spin Hall prediction) was quickly confirmed quantitatively by the HgTe conductance quantization, and the field is now central to condensed matter, with strong first-principles and spectroscopic follow-up. Complements the 2016 topological-phase prize without duplicating it.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the decisive Z2 theory and the graphene quantum spin Hall proposal; Molenkamp led the experimental realization in HgTe (following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, whose authors are not in the credited names). Hasan's 3D topological insulator ARPES work is an additional claimant I leave out under the three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than fifteen years of independent confirmation in several material families, with stable interpretation, so timing is good.
uncertainties: Credit among Kane-Mele, Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Fu-Kane-Mele and Hasan is genuinely split and the three-person cap forces a cut.
Overlap with the other topological-insulator candidates on the longlist (B004, B037) means the committee must choose one framing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moire flat-band physics: correlated insulators, superconductivity and later topological states in a tunable two-dimensional platform. This is a striking case of a theoretical flat-band prediction being met by experiment, and of a 2D material surprising us again.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle from a continuum model; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states. Prediction plus discovery gives a clean theory-experiment prize configuration, though Cao and others on the experiment side are not credited in this entry.
assessment.maturity: Highly replicated across many groups, with an enormous follow-on literature; interpretation of the superconducting mechanism is still evolving, but the discovery itself is solid.
uncertainties: Origin of the superconductivity is not settled.
Experimental credit is concentrated on a group; the supplied names omit the first author and other contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance and the giant MgO-barrier TMR are physically clear spin-dependent tunnelling effects with large practical impact (read heads, MRAM). The coherent-tunnelling picture in epitaxial MgO is well explained by band-structure calculations, which is the kind of theory-experiment link I value.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin (and the Yuasa/Djayaprawira group, not credited here) established giant MgO TMR. The three names give a reasonable configuration, though the MgO step is arguably split between Parkin and others outside the list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, widely used in technology for years; recognition adjacent to the 2007 GMR prize and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should reward the 1995 discovery or the MgO coherent-tunnelling step, and who belongs to which.
Closeness to the GMR prize may be read as a continuation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetic skyrmions are topologically protected spin textures with emergent electrodynamics, a conceptual advance in magnetism with a link to spintronic ideas. The neutron-scattering observation of the skyrmion lattice in MnSi and real-space imaging in chiral magnets are quantitatively understood.
assessment.attribution: Pfleiderer's group observed the skyrmion lattice in MnSi by neutrons (Muhlbauer et al.); Tokura's group provided real-space imaging and room-temperature materials. The theoretical prediction (Bogdanov and colleagues, Rossler) is not among the credited names, which weakens the attribution.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed in many materials, though the technological payoff (racetrack devices) has not materialized, which tempers timing.
uncertainties: Credit to the theoretical predecessors is missing from the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory transformed the treatment of strongly correlated electrons and, combined with DFT, is the practical route to quantitative predictions for correlated materials. It is close to my own field and has had large lasting impact on how Mott physics is computed.
assessment.attribution: Georges and Kotliar built the DMFT mapping onto impurity problems, and Vollhardt (with Metzner) introduced the infinite-dimension limit; Metzner is not credited here, which leaves a real attribution gap. Georges, Kotliar and Vollhardt are still a defensible trio from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely validated, although as a method it is judged more by its success in explaining materials than by one decisive discovery.
uncertainties: Method rather than discovery: the Nobel bar for a computational theory is debatable.
Metzner's role in the infinite-dimension limit is not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Altermagnetism identifies a third collinear magnetic class with spin-split bands and zero net magnetization, a genuinely new symmetry-based concept in magnetism with spintronic promise. Of high interest for a theoretical magnetism specialist.
assessment.attribution: The classification and prediction are credited to Smejkal, Sinova and Jungwirth, with earlier related ideas from other groups (Hayami, Yuan, Naka and others) that are not credited; attribution may be contested.
assessment.maturity: Recent (about 2022 onward) with ARPES and other confirmations in MnTe and CrSb emerging; probably premature for now, but a strong future candidate.
uncertainties: Short confirmation history; spectroscopic evidence is still accumulating.
Priority disputes over earlier work on spin-split antiferromagnets.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Spin-orbit torques allow electrical switching of magnetization without spin-polarized injection, with clear device relevance for MRAM. Physics rests on spin Hall and Rashba-type interfacial effects, which I would want to see separated with quantitative theory.
assessment.attribution: Miron and Gambardella showed switching in Pt/Co/AlOx; Buhrman demonstrated spin Hall torque switching. The relative roles of bulk spin Hall effect and interface Rashba effect remain mixed, and Dyakonov, Hirsch and others who predicted the spin Hall effect are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Mature in experiment with industrial development, but microscopic interpretation is still debated.
uncertainties: Spin Hall versus interfacial origin is not fully settled.
Theoretical origin credit is outside the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-resolution RIXS turned a photon-hungry probe into a quantitative tool for magnetic and orbital excitations in quantum materials, directly tied to synchrotron facilities like those I work with from the theory side. Strong in impact on correlated electron physics, yet it is an experimental technique rather than a single new phenomenon.
assessment.attribution: Ghiringhelli and Braicovich developed the instrumentation (ERIXS and related) and showed paramagnons in cuprates; Keimer is a leading user but more a materials physicist than an instrument developer, so the fairness of the trio is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Mature and increasingly important with new sources, though instrument developments are often judged less decisive for the Nobel Prize.
uncertainties: Whether Keimer's contribution is decisive for the method.
